newsitem.title: FRANCE: Sabotage disrupts telephone network in Algiers.
newsitem.headline: Sabotage disrupts telephone network in Algiers.

text.p: Algerian telecommunication authorities on Monday acknowledged for the first time that Moslem fundamentalist violence had disrupted the Algiers telephone system.
It said "successive acts of vandalism", the official term used to describe Moslem guerrilla sabotage, had caused havoc in the telephone network in the Algiers borough of Hussein Dey.
The authorities said in a statement read on Algerian state-run radio that repair crews were working to fix the damage.
The capital has experienced sporadic gas and electricity shortages in the past year because of what residents said were similar acts of sabotage.
The Algerian government blames Moslem guerrillas for a sabotage campaign which it says has inflicted losses on the economy totalling more than $2.0 billion.
